gen-fs-zina-fs-sentient: Sharp, fine-haired and striking. Zina's fat downstrokes and threadlike upstrokes sit over Sentient, a text serif whose thick-thin shift is far more measured, comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-zina-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One reads slowly and curvily, thin joins as sturdy as its stems, like a leisurely walk. Zina is the sharper foil above it, so a long passage would feel unhurried, with dark strokes giving way to hairlines.
gen-fugaz-one-fs-rowan: Fugaz One looks like bent paperclip wire, with narrow margins between letters. Rowan, a text serif with generous curve openings and gently restrained swelling, stays friendly across a longer stretch, though it isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-general-sans-fs-erode: Erode reads like a dignified page, with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders, its stroke weight shifting just enough to notice. General Sans handles the rod-stock sharpness of a heading, and Erode does the gentle, flowing work of the text.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-general-sans: General Sans carries the text with a steady pressure, like a fixed-width nib, and a tall x-height that fills the line. Abyssinica SIL, with its short ascenders and big bowls, feels dignified next to it, moderate in contrast where the sans stays level.
gen-gf-amiri-quran-fs-bespoke-sans: Dignified and bookish. Amiri Quran does best with gentle thickening and compact, knitted strands of letters, while Bespoke Sans does best with sharp, plain shapes and generous space around each curve.
gen-gf-arbutus-general-sans: Arbutus brings big counters and a spread-out, friendly look with mild stroke contrast. And General Sans follows with steady pressure and diagonals as hefty as its stems, so a longer passage moves smoothly around each bend.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-alpino: Expressive, with a laser-etched trace running through every letter of Autour One. Alpino does the quieter job, a cozy, casual sans whose tall body makes ascenders look short and keeps curve endings well apart.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-paquito: Autour One makes an o with sides and top equally thick, bold and expressive. And Paquito, a confident serif with barely any gap between x-height and caps, keeps the page approachable beneath it.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-ranade: Autour One is bold and expressive, drawn with no hairline-to-stem shift at all. Its strongest quality is the flat, uniform stroke, which Ranade, a sans with slight rubber-cord shading and widely spaced type, softens beautifully.
